title: progressive-hybrid-shadow-promote-with-fidelity-gates
author: Maya Velazquez
description: Motivation: Improve our model promotion story by running high-fidelity shadow traffic comparisons and progressively promoting models from shadow -> canary -> full based on both fidelity and operational metrics. This PR introduces a lightweight 'fidelity gate' service that scores shadow responses against production baselines, new wiring in the servegraph to support hybrid shadow+canary lanes, and a promotion controller that performs staged ramping with automatic rollback when fidelity or SLO gates fail. Key constraints: non-disruptive to existing traffic routing, minimal added latency to the control plane, and clear observability for on-call. Changes include: 1) fidelity-gate service and scoring adapters; 2) servegraph route extensions to attach shadow lanes with sampling and response capture; 3) promotion-controller that drives staged weight increases, evaluates fidelity/latency/error budgets, and triggers rollback snapshots; 4) e2e smoke harness and replay simulator for local validation; 5) instrumentation and new telemetry buckets (fidelity.score, fidelity.delta_histogram). Checklist: - [x] fidelity service prototype and unit tests - [x] servegraph integration and backwards-compatible config flags - [x] promotion controller with canary holdpoints and rollback snapshots - [x] end-to-end smoke and replay tests (simulated production traces) - [x] dashboards and alert rules added - [x] documentation draft for runbooks and Linear tickets. Related: ENG-4521 (promotion controller design), ENG-4590 (servegraph shadow plumbing), SUP-203 (customer-driven shadow request). Rollout plan: deploy fidelity-gate as opt-in behind feature flag; enable hybrid shadow lanes for a small cohort; run comparative replay for 48 hours before auto-promotion opt-in. Testing: unit, integration, synthetic traffic replay, and a limited staged rollout to a dogfood account. Risks and mitigations: transient false positives from scoring are smoothed by an annealing window and require sustained degradation for rollback; added control-plane load is bounded by a sampling quota and cache layers. Merge method: squash and merge.

Backwards-compatible and behind feature flags.
